n.1: Soil type is kept the same in every pot, so it is a controlled variable.
n.2: Fertilizer mass is the independent variable: the factor the student deliberately changes.
n.3: Daily water is held constant, so it is a controlled variable.

S.q: A lab thermometer is checked in a water bath held at exactly 50.0 °C. Readings: Trial 1, 47.1 °C; Trial 2, 47.0 °C; Trial 3, 47.2 °C. Which statement best describes the thermometer?
o: It is neither accurate nor precise.
It is accurate but not precise.
It is precise but not accurate.
It is both accurate and precise.
S.w: Precision is how close repeated readings are to each other; these agree within 0.2 °C, so they are precise. Accuracy is closeness to the true value; all three are about 3 °C low, so the thermometer is not accurate (a systematic error, such as poor calibration).

n.0: The readings agree within 0.2 °C of each other, so they are precise.
n.1: This swaps the terms: the readings agree closely with each other (precise) but sit far from 50.0 °C (not accurate).
n.3: Readings 3 °C below the known temperature are not accurate, however tightly they cluster.

S.q: A traveler returns from a tropical region with cycles of fever and chills and is diagnosed with malaria. Which statement correctly identifies the cause and how it spread?
o: A bacterium, spread through contaminated drinking water
A bacterium, spread by the bite of infected deer ticks
A virus, spread by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes
A protozoan, spread by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes
S.w: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium, a single-celled eukaryote. The female Anopheles mosquito is the vector that carries it, not the cause.

n.0: Malaria is vector-borne; waterborne protozoan illness is giardiasis.
n.1: Ticks spread Lyme disease, caused by the bacterium Borrelia burgdorferi, not malaria.
n.2: The mosquito is the correct vector, but the pathogen is a protozoan, not a virus.

S.q: A red blood cell leaves the left ventricle, travels to a capillary in the big toe and eventually returns to the left ventricle. Which capillary beds does it pass through, and in what order?
o: Two beds: the toe, then the pulmonary capillaries
Three beds: the toe, the coronary bed, then the lungs
Two beds: the pulmonary capillaries, then the toe
One bed: the systemic capillaries in the toe
S.w: Step 1: from the left ventricle the cell goes through systemic arteries to the toe capillaries, then back by veins to the right atrium. Step 2: the right ventricle sends it to the pulmonary capillaries, and the pulmonary veins return it to the left atrium and left ventricle. Two beds, systemic first.

n.1: The coronary bed is a separate branch of the systemic circuit, not a stop on the route to and from the toe.
n.2: Leaving the left ventricle, it enters the systemic circuit first; the lungs come after the right ventricle.
n.3: To get back to the left ventricle it must also pass through the lungs, a second capillary bed.

S.q: A urinalysis shows large amounts of protein and many red blood cells. Select the structure whose damage most likely allowed them into the filtrate.

sn.desc: Descending limb of the loop of Henle

S.w: Filtration happens in the renal corpuscle: blood pressure in the glomerular capillaries pushes water and small solutes into the capsule. The glomerular filtration barrier normally holds back blood cells and large plasma proteins, so finding them in urine points to glomerular damage.

n.pct: The PCT reabsorbs from the filtrate. Red blood cells and large proteins reach it only if the filter upstream has failed.
n.desc: The descending limb reabsorbs water from filtrate that has already formed. It plays no part in deciding what is filtered.
n.ptc: The peritubular capillaries take back reabsorbed substances from the tubule. They are not the filtering capillaries.
n.cd: The collecting duct receives filtrate at the end of the tubule and adjusts water. It plays no part in filtration.

S.q: After four weeks, a researcher calculates the mean height of the plants in each fertilizer group and plots the means on a bar graph. She has not yet decided what the results mean. Which step is she performing?
o: Drawing a conclusion
Analyzing the data
Conducting the experiment
Forming a hypothesis
S.w: Calculating means and graphing them is data analysis. Deciding whether the results support the hypothesis, the conclusion, comes next.

n.0: The conclusion is the decision about whether the data support the hypothesis, which she has not made yet.
n.2: Conducting the experiment was the four weeks of growing and measuring; summarizing those numbers is analysis.
n.3: The hypothesis was formed before the plants were grown.

S.q: A patient is asked to rise up onto the toes. Which movement occurs at the ankle, and which muscles act as the prime movers?
o: Plantar flexion by the tibialis anterior
Dorsiflexion by the gastrocnemius and soleus
Dorsiflexion by the tibialis anterior
Plantar flexion by the gastrocnemius and soleus
S.w: Step 1: rising onto the toes points the foot downward, which is plantar flexion. Step 2: the prime movers of plantar flexion are the gastrocnemius and soleus, acting through the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.

n.0: The tibialis anterior produces dorsiflexion, not plantar flexion.
n.1: The gastrocnemius and soleus plantar flex the ankle; dorsiflexion is the action of the tibialis anterior.
n.2: Dorsiflexion lifts the toes toward the shin, the opposite of rising onto the toes.

S.q: A student tests whether water temperature affects how long a sugar cube takes to dissolve, using water at 20 °C, 40 °C and 60 °C. Which factors should she hold constant in every trial? Select all that apply.
o: Time for the cube to dissolve
Rate of stirring
Temperature of the water
Mass of the sugar cube
Volume of water used
S.w: Controlled variables are everything except the independent variable that could affect the dependent variable: sugar mass, water volume and stirring rate. Keeping them the same makes temperature the only possible cause of differences.

n.0: Dissolving time is the dependent variable that she measures, so it is expected to change.
n.2: Water temperature is the independent variable; it must change between trials.

S.q: Activity of a human enzyme at five temperatures: 20 °C, 15 units; 30 °C, 30 units; 37 °C, 42 units; 45 °C, 20 units; 55 °C, 3 units. What is the best prediction for activity at 65 °C?
o: Lower than at 55 °C, since activity falls past the optimum
About 42 units, since the enzyme has hit its maximum
Higher than at 55 °C, since the activity cycles up and down
Higher than at 37 °C, since heat speeds up reactions
S.w: Enzyme activity rises to an optimum (37 °C here) and then falls as heat denatures the enzyme. Activity is already only 3 units at 55 °C, so at 65 °C it should be even lower, close to zero.

n.1: The maximum of 42 units occurred at 37 °C; activity has fallen steeply since then.
n.2: The data show a rise-then-fall pattern, not a repeating cycle.
n.3: Heat speeds reactions only up to the optimum; above it the enzyme denatures and activity drops, as the data show.

S.q: In a leaf cell, water molecules are split and oxygen gas is released during photosynthesis. Where in the chloroplast does this happen?
o: In the inner membrane, during electron transport
In the thylakoids, during the light reactions
In the cytoplasm, during glycolysis
In the stroma, during the Calvin cycle
S.w: The light-dependent reactions take place in the thylakoid membranes. There water is split, O₂ is released, and ATP and NADPH are made for the Calvin cycle.

n.0: Electron transport on an inner membrane that ends with O₂ forming water describes mitochondria, the reverse of releasing O₂.
n.2: Glycolysis in the cytoplasm is part of respiration and neither splits water nor releases oxygen.
n.3: The Calvin cycle in the stroma fixes CO₂ into sugar; it does not split water.

S.q: A biopsy from the sole of the foot shows a clear layer of flattened dead cells between the stratum granulosum and the stratum corneum. A biopsy from the upper arm lacks it. Which layer is this?
o: Papillary layer
Stratum spinosum
Stratum basale
Stratum lucidum
S.w: The stratum lucidum is a thin, clear layer between the granulosum and corneum that is present in the thick skin of the palms and soles and absent from thin skin.

n.0: The papillary layer is the superficial part of the dermis, below the whole epidermis.
n.1: The stratum spinosum lies below the granulosum and is present in both thick and thin skin.
n.2: The stratum basale is the deepest epidermal layer and is present in all skin.

S.q: Silicon, used in computer chips, is located in period 3 of the periodic table. What does the period number tell you about the structure of a silicon atom?
o: It has three valence electrons
It forms ions with a charge of 3+
It is third from the top in its group
Its electrons occupy three shells
S.w: The period (row) number equals the number of occupied electron shells. Silicon (14 electrons) is arranged 2, 8, 4: three shells, with 4 valence electrons.

n.0: The number of valence electrons comes from the group, not the period. Silicon is in group 14 and has 4 valence electrons.
n.1: The period number does not give an ion's charge, and silicon, with 4 valence electrons, does not typically form 3+ ions.
n.2: Silicon is second in group 14, below carbon. The period number refers to shells, not position within a group.

S.q: After several hours of hiking without water, Grace becomes dehydrated and her ADH secretion rises. How does this change the urine her kidneys produce?
o: Smaller volume of more dilute urine
Smaller volume of more concentrated urine
Larger volume of urine containing more sodium
Larger volume of more dilute urine
S.w: ADH (antidiuretic hormone) makes the collecting ducts reabsorb more water, so the kidneys produce a smaller volume of more concentrated urine.

n.0: Reabsorbing more water leaves the remaining urine more concentrated, not more dilute.
n.2: ADH reduces urine volume; increased sodium and water loss is the effect of ANP from the heart.
n.3: This is the effect of low ADH; ADH is anti-diuretic, so it reduces urine output.

S.q: A science club is choosing a question for its next investigation. Which claim can be investigated scientifically?
o: Schools should require students to sleep 8 hours a night.
Dreams carry hidden messages that no measurement can detect.
Students ought to value sleep more than late-night study.
Students who sleep 8 hours score higher on memory tests.
S.w: Scientific claims must be testable and falsifiable with empirical evidence. Sleep hours and memory scores can both be measured and compared.

n.0: This is a policy recommendation about what ought to happen; data can inform it, but no observation can test an 'ought'.
n.1: A claim defined as undetectable by any measurement cannot be falsified, so it cannot be investigated scientifically.
n.2: This is a value judgment about what students should care about, which cannot be measured objectively.

S.q: Which type of tissue forms the intervertebral discs and the menisci of the knee, where it resists compression and absorbs shock between bones?
o: Hyaline cartilage
Dense regular connective tissue
Fibrocartilage
Elastic cartilage
S.w: Fibrocartilage is the strongest, most shock-absorbing cartilage, with thick collagen bundles. It forms the intervertebral discs, the knee menisci and the pubic symphysis.

n.0: Hyaline cartilage covers articular surfaces and forms costal cartilage and growth plates; it is not the disc or meniscus tissue.
n.1: Dense regular connective tissue forms tendons and ligaments, not the discs or menisci.
n.3: Elastic cartilage gives flexible support in the ear auricle and epiglottis.

S.q: A tumor near the base of the brain disrupts a patient's body temperature control, thirst and pituitary hormone secretion. Which single structure is most likely affected?
o: Thalamus
Pineal gland
Medulla oblongata
Hypothalamus
S.w: The hypothalamus regulates body temperature, hunger, thirst and water balance and controls the pituitary gland, so one lesion there explains all three problems.

n.0: The thalamus relays sensory information to the cortex; it does not control temperature, thirst or the pituitary.
n.1: The pineal gland secretes melatonin for the sleep-wake cycle.
n.2: The medulla oblongata controls heart rate, breathing and blood pressure, not thirst or pituitary secretion.

S.q: A student is filling in a chart that compares DNA with RNA. Which features do DNA and RNA have in common? Select all that apply.
o: The sugar deoxyribose in each nucleotide
The base uracil in place of thymine
A double-stranded helical shape
Phosphate groups in the backbone
The bases guanine and cytosine
The base adenine
S.w: Both nucleic acids have a sugar-phosphate backbone and the bases A, G and C. DNA has deoxyribose and thymine and is double-stranded; RNA has ribose and uracil and is usually single-stranded.

n.0: Deoxyribose is found in DNA only; RNA contains ribose.
n.1: Uracil is found in RNA, where it replaces the thymine of DNA.
n.2: DNA is a double helix, but RNA is usually single-stranded.

S.q: A student is reviewing the features of spongy (cancellous) bone. Which statements about spongy bone are accurate? Select all that apply.
o: Its spaces hold red marrow in flat bones
It forms the dense outer wall of the diaphysis
It fills the epiphyses of long bones
Its basic units are tightly packed osteons
It is built from a lattice of trabeculae
S.w: Spongy bone is a lighter network of trabeculae whose spaces hold red marrow. It fills the epiphyses of long bones and the interior of flat bones and vertebrae. Compact bone, built of osteons, forms the dense outer layer, including the wall of the diaphysis.

n.1: The dense outer wall of the diaphysis is compact (cortical) bone; spongy bone is light and porous.
n.3: Osteons (Haversian systems) are the units of compact bone; spongy bone is organized as trabeculae without osteons.

S.q: A 54-gram metal sample is lowered into a graduated cylinder, and the water level rises from 30.0 mL to 50.0 mL. What is the density of the metal in grams per milliliter? Enter your answer rounded to the nearest tenth.

tr.1.8: Divided by the starting water level (30 mL) instead of the volume displaced.
tr.1.1: Divided by the final water level (50 mL) instead of the volume displaced.
tr.0.4: Divided volume by mass (20 / 54) instead of mass by volume.

S.w: Step 1: volume by water displacement = 50.0 mL - 30.0 mL = 20.0 mL. Step 2: density = mass / volume = 54 g / 20.0 mL = 2.7 g/mL.

S.q: Place the structures in the order deoxygenated blood returning from the lower body passes through them, starting with the first.
o: Right ventricle
Pulmonary valve
Tricuspid valve
Pulmonary artery
Inferior vena cava
Right atrium
S.w: Blood from the lower body returns in the inferior vena cava to the right atrium, passes the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, then leaves through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk and pulmonary arteries to the lungs.

S.q: A few drops of phenolphthalein indicator are added to a clear, colorless solution, and the solution turns pink. Which of these could the solution be?
o: Distilled water
Dilute sodium hydroxide
Carbonated water
Dilute acetic acid (vinegar)
S.w: Phenolphthalein is colorless in acidic and neutral solutions and turns pink in basic solutions. Sodium hydroxide is a strong base.

n.0: Pure water is neutral (pH 7), so phenolphthalein stays colorless.
n.2: Carbonated water contains carbonic acid, so it is acidic and the indicator stays colorless.
n.3: Vinegar is acidic, so phenolphthalein stays colorless.

S.q: A chemistry student needs to dispense small liquid volumes with high precision during a titration lab. Which items are designed for precise volume measurement? Select all that apply.
o: Erlenmeyer flask
Pipette
Burette
Test tube
Volumetric flask
Beaker
S.w: Burettes (used in titration), pipettes and volumetric flasks are calibrated for precise volumes. A volumetric flask holds one exact volume; a pipette and burette deliver small precise volumes.

n.0: An Erlenmeyer flask is a container for swirling and mixing; its markings are approximate.
n.3: A test tube is a container for small samples and reactions, not a measuring tool.
n.5: A beaker is for holding, mixing and heating; its markings give a rough volume.

S.q: Place these events of a typical 28-day ovarian and uterine cycle in order, starting with day 1 of the cycle.
o: Estrogen from growing follicles rebuilds the endometrium (proliferative phase)
The functional layer of the endometrium is shed (menstrual phase)
An LH surge causes the dominant follicle to release a secondary oocyte
The corpus luteum degenerates and progesterone levels fall
Progesterone from the corpus luteum makes the endometrium secretory
S.w: Days 1 to 5: menstrual phase, as the functional layer is shed. Days 6 to 14: FSH-stimulated follicles secrete estrogen that rebuilds the endometrium (proliferative phase). About day 14: high estrogen triggers the LH surge and ovulation. Days 15 to 28: the corpus luteum secretes progesterone and the endometrium is secretory. Without pregnancy, the corpus luteum degenerates near the end of the cycle, progesterone falls, and menstruation begins again.

S.q: When a DNA sample is gently heated, its two strands separate, yet each strand's sugar-phosphate backbone stays intact. Which bonds were broken?
o: Glycosidic bonds between the sugars
Peptide bonds between nucleotides
Hydrogen bonds between paired bases
Phosphodiester bonds in the backbone
S.w: The two strands are held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary bases (2 for A-T, 3 for G-C). The backbone is held by strong covalent phosphodiester bonds, which stay intact.

n.0: Glycosidic bonds join sugars in carbohydrates; DNA strands are not held together this way.
n.1: Peptide bonds join amino acids in proteins, not nucleotides.
n.3: Phosphodiester bonds form the backbone, which the stem says stayed intact.

S.q: A student mixes two clear, colorless solutions in a test tube. Within seconds, a cloudy yellow solid forms and slowly settles to the bottom. What does this observation most likely indicate?
o: A chemical change, because a precipitate has formed
A physical change, because two liquids were mixed
A physical change, because the solid can be filtered off
A chemical change, because the mixture is now uneven
S.w: The formation of a precipitate (an insoluble solid) from two solutions is a sign of a chemical change: a new substance with new properties has been produced. Other signs include unexpected gas, color change, light and temperature change.

n.1: Mixing alone can be physical, but here a new solid substance appeared, which signals a reaction.
n.2: Being able to separate the solid by filtration does not make the change physical; the solid is a newly formed substance.
n.3: The change is chemical, but the reason is the new substance; a heterogeneous mixture can also form by purely physical mixing.

S.q: Copper is drawn into thin wires for electrical cables and conducts electricity very well. Which type of bonding between copper atoms explains these properties?
o: Metallic bonding, with delocalized electrons moving among cations
Hydrogen bonding, with weak attractions between copper atoms
Covalent bonding, with electron pairs shared between copper atoms
Ionic bonding, with electrons transferred between copper atoms
S.w: In metallic bonding, metal cations sit in a sea of delocalized electrons. The mobile electrons carry current, and the cations can slide past one another without breaking the bond, which makes metals ductile and malleable.

n.1: Hydrogen bonds need hydrogen bonded to N, O or F; they do not form between copper atoms.
n.2: Localized shared pairs would not let electrons flow freely or let layers slide, so covalent bonding cannot explain conduction and ductility.
n.3: Ionic bonds form between a metal and a nonmetal; identical copper atoms do not transfer electrons to one another.

S.q: A newborn is protected against several infections for the first few months of life by antibodies received from the mother before birth. Which antibody class provides this protection?
o: IgA
IgM
IgE
IgG
S.w: IgG is the only antibody class that crosses the placenta, giving the fetus naturally acquired passive immunity that fades over weeks to months after birth.

n.0: IgA reaches the infant in breast milk after birth, not across the placenta before birth.
n.1: IgM is a large pentamer that does not cross the placenta; it is the first antibody made in a primary response.
n.2: IgE binds mast cells and basophils in allergy and parasite defense; it does not cross the placenta.

S.q: Two parents are both carriers of cystic fibrosis, an autosomal recessive disorder. What is the probability that their next child will also be a carrier? Enter your answer as a whole-number percent.

tr.25: gave the chance of an affected (ff) child
tr.67: gave the carrier share among unaffected children only
tr.75: gave the chance of an unaffected child

S.w: Ff x Ff gives 1 FF : 2 Ff : 1 ff. Carriers are Ff, so the probability is 2/4 = 1/2 = 50%.

S.q: Which sweat glands are distributed over most of the body surface, open directly onto the skin through pores, and secrete watery sweat that cools the body?
o: Sebaceous glands
Eccrine glands
Ceruminous glands
Apocrine glands
S.w: Eccrine (merocrine) sweat glands are the most numerous, are found almost everywhere (especially palms, soles and forehead), open onto the surface through pores and secrete watery sweat for thermoregulation.

n.0: Sebaceous glands secrete oily sebum, usually into hair follicles; they do not produce sweat.
n.2: Ceruminous glands are modified sweat glands in the ear canal that produce earwax.
n.3: Apocrine glands are found in the axillary and anogenital regions, open into hair follicles and become active at puberty.

S.q: Most homeostatic mechanisms use negative feedback, but a few use positive feedback. Which of the following is an example of positive feedback?
o: Oxytocin release that strengthens uterine contractions in labor
A slower heart rate that lowers a sudden rise in blood pressure
Insulin release that lowers blood glucose after a meal
Shivering that raises body temperature when it falls
S.w: During childbirth, pressure on the cervix triggers oxytocin release, which strengthens contractions, which triggers more oxytocin. The change is amplified until the baby is delivered.

n.1: The baroreceptor reflex reverses a rise in blood pressure, which is negative feedback.
n.2: Insulin reverses a rise in blood glucose, which is negative feedback.
n.3: Shivering reverses a fall in body temperature, which is negative feedback.

S.q: A survey of 2,000 nursing students finds that those who drink more energy drinks also report higher anxiety levels. Which conclusion is justified by this survey?
o: Cutting out energy drinks will lower students' anxiety.
Energy drinks cause anxiety in nursing students.
Anxiety causes students to drink more energy drinks.
Energy-drink use and anxiety are linked in this group.
S.w: A survey is observational: it shows an association (correlation) but cannot show which variable causes which, or whether a third factor, such as exam stress, drives both.

n.0: This predicts the effect of an intervention, which requires evidence of causation.
n.1: Concluding causation from a correlation is the classic error; only a controlled experiment can show it.
n.2: Reversing the direction is still a causal claim the survey cannot support.

S.q: Two glucose molecules are joined to form the disaccharide maltose. Which description of this reaction is correct?
o: A water molecule is released, forming a peptide bond.
A water molecule is released, forming a glycosidic bond.
A water molecule is added, forming a peptide bond.
A water molecule is added, forming a glycosidic bond.
S.w: Monomers are joined by dehydration synthesis, which releases water. Bonds between sugars are glycosidic bonds.

n.0: Peptide bonds join amino acids, not sugars.
n.2: This combines both errors: adding water breaks bonds, and peptide bonds join amino acids.
n.3: Adding water is hydrolysis, which breaks polymers apart rather than joining them.

S.q: A meal contains bread, lean turkey and butter. When the resulting chyme first enters the duodenum, which statement about the chemical digestion of this meal is accurate?
o: Protein digestion has begun; starch and fat digestion have not
Starch and protein digestion have begun; most fat digestion has not
Starch digestion has begun; protein and fat digestion have not
Fat and protein digestion have begun; starch digestion has not
S.w: Step 1: starch digestion begins in the mouth with salivary amylase. Step 2: protein digestion begins in the stomach with pepsin. Fat digestion is mostly in the small intestine, after bile and pancreatic lipase act (lingual lipase does very little), so most fat digestion has not yet occurred.

n.0: Starch digestion began in the mouth with salivary amylase, before the stomach.
n.2: Protein digestion has already begun in the stomach by the time chyme reaches the duodenum.
n.3: Most fat digestion waits for bile and pancreatic lipase in the small intestine, while starch digestion began in the mouth.

S.q: At rest, the inside of a typical neuron is about -70 mV relative to the outside. Which mechanism uses ATP directly to help maintain this resting membrane potential?
o: Na⁺/K⁺ pump moving 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in
Voltage-gated Na⁺ channels letting Na⁺ flow in
Ca²⁺ channels letting Ca²⁺ into the axon terminal
Na⁺/K⁺ pump moving 2 Na⁺ out and 3 K⁺ in
S.w: The sodium-potassium pump uses ATP to move 3 Na⁺ out of the cell and 2 K⁺ in. Together with K⁺ leak channels, this keeps the inside of the resting neuron negative.

n.1: Voltage-gated Na⁺ channels open at threshold and cause depolarization; they are passive channels, not an ATP-driven pump.
n.2: Ca²⁺ channels at the axon terminal open during synaptic transmission; they do not maintain the resting potential.
n.3: The ratio is reversed: the pump moves 3 Na⁺ out and 2 K⁺ in.

S.q: A student rests a hand on her abdomen and feels it move outward during a normal, quiet inspiration. What is her diaphragm doing at that moment?
o: It relaxes and flattens, which lets the ribs fall and draws air in
It contracts, flattens and moves downward, enlarging the thoracic cavity
It contracts and domes upward, which pushes air into the lungs
It relaxes and domes upward, which enlarges the thoracic cavity
S.w: In inspiration the diaphragm contracts, flattens and moves down, increasing the vertical size of the thoracic cavity. The larger volume lowers pressure in the lungs, so air flows in.

n.0: A relaxed diaphragm domes upward rather than flattening, and falling ribs reduce thoracic volume.
n.2: A contracting diaphragm flattens and moves down; it does not dome upward or push air.
n.3: Relaxing and doming upward is what the diaphragm does in expiration, and it makes the thoracic cavity smaller.

S.q: A patient breathes in oxygen that eventually reaches the mitochondria of her cells. What is the role of this oxygen in aerobic cellular respiration?
o: It accepts electrons from the chain and forms water.
It is released as a product of the light reactions.
It splits glucose into two molecules of pyruvate.
It combines with carbon to form carbon dioxide.
S.w: Oxygen is the final electron acceptor of the electron transport chain; it picks up electrons and hydrogen ions to form water.

n.1: Release of oxygen by the light reactions is part of photosynthesis, not respiration.
n.2: Glycolysis splits glucose into pyruvate without using any oxygen.
n.3: The CO₂ exhaled comes from carbon in glucose released during pyruvate oxidation and the Krebs cycle, not from the oxygen breathed in.

S.q: In a healthy person at rest, which change in the blood is the strongest stimulus to increase the rate and depth of breathing?
o: A fall in oxygen, sensed by the central chemoreceptors
A fall in carbon dioxide, sensed as a rise in pH
A rise in oxygen, sensed by the carotid bodies
A rise in carbon dioxide, sensed as a fall in pH
S.w: Rising CO₂ is the main everyday drive to breathe. CO₂ forms carbonic acid, lowering the pH of cerebrospinal fluid, which central chemoreceptors in the medulla detect.

n.0: Low oxygen is a weaker, backup stimulus in healthy people, and it is sensed by peripheral chemoreceptors, not central ones.
n.1: Falling CO₂ and rising pH slow breathing rather than speed it up.
n.2: A rise in oxygen would not drive breathing up; the carotid bodies respond to a fall in O₂.

S.q: Six primary oocytes and six primary spermatocytes complete meiosis normally, and each oocyte is fertilized so that meiosis II finishes. How many ova and how many sperm result in total?
o: 6 ova and 24 sperm
6 ova and 12 sperm
24 ova and 24 sperm
12 ova and 24 sperm
S.w: Two steps. (1) Oogenesis divides the cytoplasm unequally, so each primary oocyte yields 1 ovum plus polar bodies: 6 x 1 = 6 ova. (2) Spermatogenesis yields 4 sperm per primary spermatocyte: 6 x 4 = 24 sperm.

n.1: This counts 2 sperm per spermatocyte, which stops after meiosis I; meiosis II gives 4 per spermatocyte.
n.2: This treats oogenesis like spermatogenesis; polar bodies are not functional ova, so each oocyte gives 1 ovum.
n.3: This counts the first polar body as a second ovum; polar bodies degenerate and are not ova.

S.q: In the reaction 2 Na + Cl₂ → 2 NaCl, each neutral sodium atom becomes a sodium ion, Na⁺. Which statement correctly describes what happens to sodium?
o: Sodium is reduced, because its charge increases
Sodium is reduced, because it loses an electron
Sodium is oxidized, because it loses an electron
Sodium is oxidized, because it gains an electron
S.w: Oxidation is loss of electrons; reduction is gain of electrons (OIL RIG). Sodium loses one electron to become Na⁺, so it is oxidized; chlorine gains the electron and is reduced.

n.0: A rising (more positive) charge means electrons were lost, which is oxidation; reduction lowers the charge.
n.1: Losing electrons is oxidation, not reduction. Reduction is the gain of electrons.
n.3: Gaining an electron would give sodium a negative charge; forming Na⁺ requires losing one.

S.q: A hiker drinks no water during a long, hot climb and becomes dehydrated, so the osmolality of his blood plasma rises. Which response should be predicted?
o: ADH secretion rises, and urine output rises and turns paler.
ADH secretion falls, and urine output falls and turns darker.
ADH secretion falls, and urine output rises and turns paler.
ADH secretion rises, and urine output falls and turns darker.
S.w: Dehydration raises plasma osmolality, which increases ADH (antidiuretic hormone) release. ADH makes the kidneys reabsorb more water, so the body produces less urine that is more concentrated and darker.

n.0: Rising ADH conserves water, so urine output falls rather than rises.
n.1: Less, darker urine is the right outcome, but it is caused by more ADH, not less.
n.2: ADH falls and urine becomes dilute when a person is overhydrated, the opposite situation.

S.q: Place these elements in order of increasing atomic radius, starting with the smallest atom.
o: Carbon
Potassium
Fluorine
Lithium
Oxygen
S.w: Fluorine, oxygen, carbon and lithium are all in period 2, where atomic radius increases from right to left (fewer protons pull the same two shells less tightly): F < O < C < Li. Potassium is in period 4, below lithium's group, and has two more occupied shells, so it is the largest.

S.q: A pea plant has purple flowers and the genotype Pp, where P (purple) is dominant over p (white). Which statement about this plant is correct?
o: It is heterozygous, and purple is its phenotype.
It is homozygous, and Pp is its phenotype.
It is heterozygous, and purple is its genotype.
It carries two different genes for flower color.
S.w: Pp has two different alleles, so the plant is heterozygous. Its genotype is Pp; its observable trait (phenotype) is purple flowers.

n.1: Homozygous means two identical alleles (PP or pp), and Pp is a genotype, not a phenotype.
n.2: Genotype and phenotype are swapped: Pp is the genotype and purple is the phenotype.
n.3: Pp is two different alleles of one gene, not two different genes.

S.q: A classmate claims that epithelial tissue and every kind of connective tissue are supplied directly by blood vessels. Which correction is accurate?
o: Bone and blood are avascular and are nourished by diffusion
Cartilage is vascular, but epithelium is nourished by diffusion
Epithelium and cartilage are both avascular and fed by diffusion
Epithelium is vascular, but cartilage is nourished by diffusion
S.w: Epithelial tissue is avascular and is fed by diffusion from underlying connective tissue. Most connective tissue is vascular, but cartilage is an avascular exception.

n.0: Bone is a vascular connective tissue, and blood flows inside vessels as the fluid connective tissue.
n.1: Cartilage is the avascular connective tissue; this option reverses the facts for both tissues.
n.3: Epithelium has no blood vessels between its cells; it relies on diffusion from the tissue below.

S.q: A cell-culture protocol calls for 0.075 L of buffer solution. The graduated cylinder on the bench is marked in milliliters. Enter the volume to measure, in milliliters, as a whole number.

tr.750: Moved the decimal point four places.
tr.7.5: Moved the decimal point only two places (multiplied by 100, the centi factor).
tr.0.000075: Divided by 1,000 instead of multiplying when going from a larger to a smaller unit.

S.w: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Converting from a larger unit (liters) to a smaller unit (milliliters) means multiplying: 0.075 x 1,000 = 75 mL. Move the decimal point three places to the right.

S.q: An infection-control handout groups diseases by the type of pathogen that causes them. Which of these diseases are caused by bacteria? Select all that apply.
o: Lyme disease
Malaria
Tuberculosis
Strep throat
Influenza
Athlete's foot
S.w: Tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis), Lyme disease (Borrelia burgdorferi, spread by ticks) and strep throat (Streptococcus pyogenes) are bacterial.

n.1: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium.
n.4: Influenza is caused by a virus.
n.5: Athlete's foot is caused by a fungus.

S.q: A patient has had most of the colon surgically removed because of disease. Which change in digestive function is most expected after the surgery?
o: Poorer uptake of vitamin B12 with intrinsic factor
Slower final breakdown of peptides by colon enzymes
Poorer absorption of glucose and amino acids
Looser stools from reduced water absorption
S.w: The large intestine's main job is absorbing water and electrolytes and forming feces. Removing most of the colon leaves less surface to reclaim water, so stools become looser.

n.0: Vitamin B12 bound to intrinsic factor is absorbed in the ileum of the small intestine, which is not part of the colon.
n.1: The large intestine has no digestive enzymes of its own; brush-border peptidases of the small intestine finish protein digestion.
n.2: Glucose and amino acids are absorbed through the villi of the small intestine; the colon has no villi and absorbs mainly water and electrolytes.

S.q: A reversible reaction in a sealed container is allowed to run until it reaches dynamic equilibrium. Which statement is true once equilibrium is reached?
o: Forward and reverse rates are equal; amounts hold steady
Reactant and product concentrations have become equal
The forward rate is faster, so products keep building up
Both reactions have stopped, so the amounts stay constant
S.w: At dynamic equilibrium the forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates, so the concentrations of reactants and products stay constant, though usually not equal to each other.

n.1: Concentrations become constant, not necessarily equal; an equilibrium mixture can be mostly products or mostly reactants.
n.2: If the forward rate were faster, the system would not yet be at equilibrium.
n.3: Amounts are constant, but both reactions keep running; equilibrium is dynamic, not stopped.

S.q: A student adds sugar to water at 25 °C and stirs for several minutes, but some sugar crystals remain undissolved on the bottom of the glass. How should the liquid in the glass be classified?
o: Saturated, so it cannot dissolve any other solute
Unsaturated, because the stirring is not yet complete
Saturated, holding the most sugar it can at 25 °C
Supersaturated, holding more sugar than its maximum
S.w: A saturated solution holds the maximum amount of a solute that can dissolve at that temperature; any extra stays undissolved. The leftover crystals show the sugar solution has reached its limit at 25 °C.

n.0: It is saturated, but a solution saturated with sugar can still dissolve other solutes, such as salt.
n.1: An unsaturated solution can still dissolve more solute; undissolved crystals after thorough stirring show it cannot.
n.3: A supersaturated solution holds more than the normal maximum with no undissolved solid; it is unstable and made by careful cooling.

S.q: During quiet, restful breathing, which muscles contract to enlarge the thoracic cavity so that air flows into the lungs?
o: External intercostals and rectus abdominis
Internal intercostals and rectus abdominis
Diaphragm and external intercostals
Diaphragm and internal intercostals
S.w: In quiet inspiration the diaphragm (the main muscle of inspiration) contracts and flattens while the external intercostals lift the ribs. Both enlarge the thoracic cavity, pressure in the lungs falls and air flows in. Quiet expiration is mostly passive recoil; the internal intercostals and abdominal muscles act in forced expiration.

n.0: The external intercostals do help, but the rectus abdominis flexes the trunk and assists forced expiration, and the diaphragm is missing.
n.1: The internal intercostals and abdominal muscles such as the rectus abdominis are muscles of forced expiration, not inspiration.
n.3: The diaphragm is right, but the internal intercostals pull the ribs down during forced expiration; they do not act in quiet inspiration.

S.q: In liver cells, the enzyme catalase greatly speeds up the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen. How does catalase increase the reaction rate?
o: It increases the total energy the reaction releases.
It is consumed and becomes part of the products.
It shifts the equilibrium toward more products.
It lowers the activation energy of the reaction.
S.w: Enzymes are biological catalysts: they lower activation energy, are not consumed, and do not change the overall energy released.

n.0: Enzymes do not change the overall energy change of the reaction, only the energy needed to start it.
n.1: Enzymes are not consumed; they are released unchanged and reused.
n.2: Enzymes do not change the equilibrium of a reaction; they help it reach equilibrium faster.

E.q: Read the sentence from a hospital policy summary: "The new policy is meant to reduce wait times, improving patient satisfaction, and to lower costs." Which revision corrects the faulty parallelism?
o: Change "to lower" to "lowering."
Change "to reduce" to "reducing."
Change "improving" to "to improve."
Delete the word "and" before "to lower."
E.w: Two of the three items are infinitives (to reduce, to lower). Changing "improving" to "to improve" makes all three match.

n.0: This leaves "to reduce" as an infinitive while the other two items are gerunds, so the list is still mixed.
n.1: This leaves "to lower" as an infinitive while the other two items are gerunds, so the list is still mixed.
n.3: Removing "and" does not change the forms of the items and also leaves the series without its conjunction.

E.q: Read the paragraph: "Community gardens offer more than fresh vegetables. Neighbors who garden together get to know one another and share skills. Gardeners also get regular outdoor exercise, and families eat more produce when they help grow it." Which sentence best concludes the paragraph?
o: Some gardeners prefer raised beds because they are easier on the back and knees.
In short, a community garden builds both good health and neighborly ties.
Vegetables such as tomatoes and peppers need at least six hours of sun each day.
However, many cities now charge a yearly fee for each garden plot in the spring.
E.w: A concluding sentence sums up the main idea without adding new information. This one ties together the social, exercise and nutrition benefits.

n.0: This sentence adds a new, minor detail instead of wrapping up the main point.
n.2: This sentence adds a new gardening fact unrelated to the benefits the paragraph lists.
n.3: This sentence introduces a new idea (fees) that the paragraph has not developed.

E.q: Read the sentence from a staff memo: "The pharmacist told the technician that her shift had been changed." Which revision makes the pronoun reference clear?
o: The pharmacist told the technician that her shift had now been changed.
The pharmacist and the technician were told that her shift changed.
The pharmacist told the technician that her own shift had been changed.
The pharmacist told the technician, "Your shift has been changed."
E.w: Turning the report into a direct quotation makes "your" refer clearly to the technician, the person being spoken to.

n.0: Adding "now" leaves "her" ambiguous; it could still mean the pharmacist's shift or the technician's.
n.1: "Her" now has two possible antecedents in the subject, so the reference is still unclear.
n.2: Adding "own" does not help: "her own" could still mean the pharmacist's shift or the technician's.

E.q: A student is writing a paragraph organized from the least to the most important point. Place the sentences in the order that creates the most logical paragraph, starting with the first sentence.
o: One benefit is simple: the rent and utility bills are split in half.
A roommate in the same program can also quiz you before major exams.
Most important, a roommate who knows long clinical days offers support when the work feels overwhelming.
Sharing an apartment with a classmate during nursing school has real advantages.
E.w: The topic sentence comes first. "One benefit" opens the list, "also" adds a second point, and "Most important" signals the final, strongest point in order-of-importance organization.

E.q: A student is checking a list of plural nouns for a biology report. Which plurals are formed correctly? Select all that apply.
o: beliefs
attorneys
passerbys
crises
wolfs
stimuluses
E.w: Crisis becomes crises (-is to -es); attorney adds s because it ends in vowel + y; belief is an f noun that simply adds s.

n.2: In a compound noun the main word is pluralized: "passersby".
n.5: Stimulus is a Latin noun whose plural is "stimuli".

E.q: A student is writing a history paper about nursing. Which sentence is capitalized correctly?
o: During the Civil War, many irish immigrants served as nurses.
During the civil war, many Irish immigrants served as nurses.
During the Civil War, many Irish Immigrants served as nurses.
During the Civil War, many Irish immigrants served as nurses.
E.w: Named historical events (the Civil War) and nationalities (Irish) are proper nouns; general nouns such as immigrants are lowercase.

n.0: Nationalities are proper adjectives, so "Irish" is capitalized.
n.1: The name of a specific historical event is capitalized: "Civil War".
n.2: "Immigrants" is a common noun and is lowercase.

E.q: A wellness coordinator is writing a poster about rest. Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
o: One factor: mattered most to the team, getting enough sleep.
One factor mattered most to the team: getting enough sleep.
One factor mattered most to the team; getting enough sleep.
The factor that mattered most was: getting enough sleep.
E.w: A colon after a complete independent clause can introduce an explanation or example: "getting enough sleep" explains the factor.

n.0: A colon must not separate a subject (One factor) from its verb (mattered).
n.2: A semicolon must join two independent clauses; "getting enough sleep" is a phrase.
n.3: A colon must not come directly after a verb such as "was".

E.q: Kiara is writing a research paper on teen vaping for her health class. Which of her activities belong to the prewriting stage? Select all that apply.
o: Formatting the final copy for submission
Building an outline of main points and support
Rewriting her conclusion so it restates the thesis
Narrowing her broad topic to a manageable focus
Correcting comma splices in her second paragraph
Gathering research on the topic before writing
E.w: Prewriting is planning: identifying purpose and audience, choosing and narrowing the topic, generating ideas, researching and outlining. Narrowing the topic, researching and outlining all happen before any drafting.

n.0: Preparing and submitting the final copy is publishing, the last stage.
n.2: Rewriting a conclusion to restate the thesis improves the content of an existing draft, which is revising.
n.4: Fixing comma splices is a sentence-level correction, which is editing.

E.q: A physical therapist is writing a home exercise plan. Which pair of words correctly completes the sentence? "The new exercise bike is ____, so it will ____ the walking program."
o: stationery; compliment
stationery; complement
stationary; compliment
stationary; complement
E.w: "Stationary" means not moving; "complement" means to complete or go well with. A bike that stays in place goes well with a walking program.

n.0: Both are wrong: the bike is stationary (not moving), and it complements (goes well with) the program.
n.1: "Stationery" is writing paper; a bike that does not move is "stationary".
n.2: "Compliment" means to praise; going well with something is "complement".

E.q: Brianna is organizing a standard five-paragraph essay for her English composition class. In which part of the essay does the thesis statement usually appear?
o: In the first sentence of the introduction
At the start of the first body paragraph
In the final sentence of the conclusion
At the end of the introduction
E.w: The introduction usually moves from a hook to background and ends with the thesis, which then leads into the body paragraphs.

n.0: The first sentence of the introduction is usually the hook that captures the reader's interest, with the thesis coming after the background.
n.1: The first body paragraph opens with a topic sentence that develops one point of the thesis; the thesis itself comes before the body.
n.2: The conclusion restates the thesis in new words; the thesis is first stated in the introduction.

E.q: A clinic notice reads: "The clinic's only X-ray machine broke down on Monday morning. ___, patients who needed imaging were sent to the hospital across town." Which transition best completes the notice?
o: As a result
Similarly
In contrast
For instance
E.w: The broken machine caused patients to be sent elsewhere, a cause-and-effect relationship. "As a result" signals an effect.

n.1: "Similarly" signals a comparison, but the second sentence describes a consequence.
n.2: "In contrast" signals a difference, but sending patients elsewhere follows from the broken machine.
n.3: "For instance" introduces an example, but sending patients away is an effect, not an example.

E.q: A nursing applicant is studying a list of commonly misspelled words before the TEAS. Which words are spelled correctly? Select all that apply.
o: embarass
occurrence
seperate
definately
privilege
accommodate
E.w: Accommodate (double c, double m), occurrence (double c, double r) and privilege (i-l-e-g-e) are correct.

n.0: The correct spelling is "embarrass", with double r and double s.
n.2: The correct spelling is "separate", with a after the p.
n.3: The correct spelling is "definitely", from the root finite.

E.q: Which working thesis needs revision because it states a fact rather than an arguable claim?
o: Bike lanes are the most cost-effective way for cities to cut traffic injuries.
Twelve-hour nursing shifts do more harm than good for patient safety.
Requiring a CPR course for graduation would make high schools safer places.
The CDC recommends that adults get at least seven hours of sleep each night.
E.w: A thesis must take a position that a reader could dispute. What the CDC recommends can be checked in a single source, so this sentence reports a fact and leaves the essay nothing to argue. The other three make judgments (more harm than good, most cost-effective, would make schools safer) that a writer would have to support.

n.0: Calling bike lanes "the most cost-effective" option is an evaluation that others could challenge with other measures, so it is arguable.
n.1: Whether long shifts do "more harm than good" is a judgment that readers could dispute, so it is an arguable claim.
n.2: Whether a CPR requirement "would make" schools safer is a debatable prediction about a policy, so it is arguable.

E.q: A school nurse is making a sign to hang above the sink in a second-grade classroom. Which sentence is most appropriate for these readers?
o: Wash your hands with soap before you eat.
Wash your hands with soap prior to consuming food.
Perform hand hygiene before you eat.
Hand washing reduces the spread of germs.
E.w: Young readers need short sentences, simple everyday words and a clear action to take.

n.1: "Prior to consuming food" is formal wording that young children may not know.
n.2: "Perform hand hygiene" is health-care jargon that seven-year-old readers may not understand.
n.3: This states a general fact but does not tell the children what to do at the sink.

E.q: A writing tutor reviews sentences from nursing students' reflection papers. Which sentences use irregular verbs correctly? Select all that apply.
o: The pipes in the old wing had froze before the heat came back on.
The intern has chose a specialty in pediatric nursing.
Ms. Reyes has led the infection control team since 2021.
The patient has already swum two laps in the therapy pool.
The phone rung three times before anyone at the desk answered.
By noon, the volunteers had drunk all of the bottled water.
E.w: Drink, drank, drunk; lead, led, led; swim, swam, swum. Each helping verb (had, has) is paired with the correct past participle.

n.0: After "had," use the past participle "frozen": "had frozen."
n.1: After "has," use the past participle "chosen": "has chosen."
n.4: The simple past of "ring" is "rang"; "rung" is the past participle and needs a helping verb.

E.q: Read the two sentences: "The clinic ran out of flu vaccine. Staff placed a new order." Which option combines them into a complex sentence?
o: The clinic ran out of flu vaccine; staff placed a new order.
When the clinic ran out of flu vaccine, staff placed a new order.
The clinic ran out of flu vaccine, so staff placed a new order.
The clinic ran out of flu vaccine and then placed a new order.
E.w: Adding the subordinating conjunction "When" turns the first clause into a dependent clause, so the result has one dependent and one independent clause: a complex sentence.

n.0: A semicolon joins two independent clauses, making a compound sentence.
n.2: A comma and "so" join two independent clauses, making a compound sentence.
n.3: This has one subject with two verbs, so it is a simple sentence (and it changes who placed the order).

E.q: Read the sentence: "The patient's fever broke overnight; therefore, the doctor canceled the blood culture." How is this sentence classified by structure?
o: Compound
Simple
Complex
Compound-complex
E.w: Both parts are independent clauses. "Therefore" is a conjunctive adverb, not a subordinating conjunction, so it does not create a dependent clause; a semicolon joins the two clauses, making the sentence compound.

n.1: There are two independent clauses, not one.
n.2: "Therefore" does not make the second clause dependent, so there is no dependent clause.
n.3: Compound-complex needs a dependent clause, and this sentence has none.

E.q: Read the sentence from a research summary: "The two surgeons collaborated together on a new protocol that cut postoperative infections by 30 percent." Which word should be deleted to remove a redundancy?
o: together
new
postoperative
two
E.w: "Collaborate" means "work together," so "collaborated together" repeats the idea. Deleting "together" removes the redundancy.

n.1: "New" tells the reader the protocol was recently created; it is not implied by any other word.
n.2: "Postoperative" names which infections were cut; deleting it would make the claim broader than the study.
n.3: "Collaborate" implies at least two people, but "two" states exactly how many surgeons, so it adds information.

E.q: A lab report described the patient's red blood cells as macrocytic. Using both the prefix and the root, what does macrocytic describe?
o: Cells that are smaller than normal
More cells than normal
Cells that are larger than normal
Fewer cells than normal
E.w: Step 1: macro- means large. Step 2: cyt/o means cell. Macrocytic therefore describes cells that are larger than normal.

n.0: Smaller than normal would be microcytic; micro- means small, the opposite of macro-.
n.1: macro- refers to size, not number; many is multi- or poly-.
n.3: A shortage of cells would use the suffix -penia (deficiency), not macro-.

E.q: Read the sentence from a discharge checklist: "The discharge packet includes: a medication list, a follow-up card, and a diet sheet." Which revision corrects the punctuation error?
o: Move the colon to follow "packet"
Replace the colon with a comma
Delete the colon after "includes"
Replace the colon with a semicolon
E.w: A colon must not separate a verb (includes) from its objects. Deleting it lets the list follow the verb directly.

n.0: A colon after "packet" would split the subject from its verb, which is also an error.
n.1: A comma must not separate a verb from its objects.
n.3: A semicolon cannot introduce a list or separate a verb from its objects.

E.q: An X-ray of the patient's stiff knee showed arthritis, and the nurse practitioner discussed treatment options with him. Based on its suffix, what does arthritis mean?
o: Surgical repair of a joint
Pain in a joint
Inflammation of a joint
A tumor of a joint
E.w: arthr/o means joint and -itis means inflammation, so arthritis is inflammation of a joint.

n.0: Surgical repair is -plasty (arthroplasty), not -itis.
n.1: Joint pain is arthralgia; pain is -algia, not -itis.
n.3: A tumor or mass is -oma, not -itis.

E.q: While revising her report on sports injuries, Hana realizes her second section lacks evidence, so she goes back to the library to find two more studies before rewriting that section. What does this show about the writing process?
o: Adding new studies is editing, so she has moved past revising
The process is recursive, so a writer may return to an earlier stage
Research is part of drafting, so she has returned to the drafting stage
The process is linear, so research must end before revising starts
E.w: The writing process is recursive: writers move back and forth between stages as needed. Hana returns to a prewriting activity (research) during revising and then continues revising, which is normal.

n.0: Editing fixes sentence-level errors such as grammar, punctuation and spelling; finding sources is a prewriting task and adding evidence changes content.
n.2: She has gone back to an earlier stage, but research is a prewriting activity, not drafting; drafting turns the plan into sentences and paragraphs.
n.3: The writing process is recursive, not linear: writers often go back to research or planning while revising, exactly as Hana does.

E.q: Read the run-on sentence from an incident report: "The power went out the generator started within seconds." Which revision corrects it?
o: The power went out, however the generator started within seconds.
The power went out, the generator started within seconds.
The power went out and, the generator started within seconds.
The power went out, and the generator started within seconds.
E.w: A comma followed by a coordinating conjunction (and) correctly joins two independent clauses.

n.0: "However" is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction, so a comma before it still leaves a comma splice.
n.1: Adding only a comma turns the run-on into a comma splice.
n.2: The comma must come before the conjunction, not after it.

E.q: Before the clinical trial began, researchers sorted the volunteers into groups so that each group was homogeneous in age. Based on its prefix, what does homogeneous mean here?
o: Different throughout
Many in number
Divided into halves
Similar throughout
E.w: homo-/homeo- means same or similar, so a group homogeneous in age is made of people of similar ages.

n.0: Different is hetero- (heterogeneous), the opposite prefix.
n.1: Many is multi- or poly-, not homo-.
n.2: Half is hemi- or semi-, not homo-.

E.q: Read the word groups from a medication note: "Because the patient was allergic to penicillin. The doctor prescribed a different antibiotic." Which revision correctly fixes the fragment?
o: Because the patient was allergic to penicillin, the doctor prescribed a different antibiotic.
Because the patient was allergic to penicillin; the doctor prescribed a different antibiotic.
Because the patient was allergic to penicillin the doctor, prescribed a different antibiotic.
The patient was allergic to penicillin, the doctor prescribed a different antibiotic.
E.w: The dependent clause (Because ... penicillin) is attached to the independent clause with a comma, giving a correct complex sentence.

n.1: A semicolon must join two independent clauses; the first part is a dependent clause.
n.2: The comma is misplaced: it separates the subject (the doctor) from its verb, and the comma after the introductory clause is missing.
n.3: Removing "Because" leaves two independent clauses joined by only a comma: a comma splice.

E.q: To plan an essay, Andre writes "sleep loss" in a circle in the center of a page, draws lines out to circles labeled "memory," "mood," and "driving," and then adds smaller circles branching from each. Which prewriting strategy is he using?
o: Clustering
Freewriting
Outlining
Listing
E.w: Clustering (also called mind mapping or webbing) puts the central topic in the middle of the page and branches related ideas out from it in linked circles.

n.1: Freewriting is writing continuous sentences for a set time; Andre is drawing linked circles, not writing prose.
n.2: Outlining arranges ideas in a labeled hierarchy (I., A., 1., a.) in lines of text, not in a web of circles around a center.
n.3: Listing jots ideas down in a vertical list; it does not connect ideas visually to a central topic.

E.q: A clinic is writing a handout for patients who have no medical training. Which sentence is best suited to these readers?
o: Pt should obtain BP readings BID and document all of the findings.
Check your blood pressure at the same time each morning and evening.
Check your systolic and diastolic pressure each morning and evening.
Patients with hypertension should monitor their BP readings diurnally.
E.w: Plain language for a lay audience uses everyday words, short sentences and clear actions, without jargon or slang.

n.0: Clinical abbreviations (Pt, BP, BID) are jargon meant for health professionals, not patients.
n.2: The action is clear, but "systolic" and "diastolic" are medical terms a lay reader may not know.
n.3: "Hypertension," "BP" and "diurnally" are technical terms a lay reader may not understand.

E.q: A receptionist is asking about a missing medical record. Which sentence uses "who's" and "whose" correctly?
o: Who's the patient who's chart is missing?
Whose the patient who's chart is missing?
Whose the patient whose chart is missing?
Who's the patient whose chart is missing?
E.w: "Who's" is the contraction of "who is" (Who is the patient?); "whose" shows possession (whose chart).

n.0: The chart belongs to the patient, so the possessive "whose" is needed, not "who is".
n.1: Both are reversed: the opening needs "who's" and the possessive needs "whose".
n.2: The sentence opens with "Who is the patient", so it needs the contraction "who's".

E.q: A mother brings her toddler to the clinic with a mild cold, a low fever, and persistent rhinorrhea. Based on its word parts, what is rhinorrhea?
o: Inflammation of the nose
A discharge from the nose
Bleeding from the nose
Surgical repair of the nose
E.w: rhin/o means nose and -rrhea means flow or discharge, so rhinorrhea is a runny nose.

n.0: Inflammation of the nose is rhinitis (-itis).
n.2: Bleeding (bursting forth) is -rrhage or -rrhagia, the look-alike suffix.
n.3: Surgical repair is -plasty (rhinoplasty).

E.q: Andre is writing a cover letter to the human resources department of a regional hospital. Which sentence is most appropriate for this letter?
o: I am eager to bring my CNA experience to your medical-surgical unit.
I'm really excited about this job, and I know I'd be a great fit.
I am, without question, the most qualified applicant you will receive.
I need a full-time job with good benefits, and your hospital offers both.
E.w: A cover letter calls for a formal, confident and respectful tone that links the applicant's experience to the employer's needs.

n.1: The contractions and the vague "great fit" are too casual and give the employer no specific reason to hire.
n.2: The boastful claim sounds arrogant and cannot be supported, which suits no professional application.
n.3: The sentence focuses on what the writer wants rather than what the writer offers the hospital.

E.q: A press release announces a new hospital wing. Which sentence uses commas correctly with the date and the place?
o: On July 4, 2026 the clinic in Austin, Texas, opened a new wing.
On July, 4, 2026, the clinic in Austin, Texas, opened a new wing.
On July 4, 2026, the clinic in Austin, Texas opened a new wing.
On July 4, 2026, the clinic in Austin, Texas, opened a new wing.
E.w: Two rules apply. In a full date, commas follow the day and the year when the sentence continues. In a city-state pair, commas follow the city and the state.

n.0: The comma after the year "2026" is missing.
n.1: No comma goes between the month and the day.
n.2: The comma after the state "Texas" is missing.

E.q: Read the passage. Select the verb that does not agree with its subject.

parts: on the top shelf. Each of the new students
a locker near the break room. A number of patients
complained about noise at night, so the safety committee
on Monday to discuss it. Neither the nurses nor the unit manager
told about the schedule change in advance.

E.w: "A number of" means several, so the subject is plural and takes a plural verb: A number of patients have complained. ("The number of" would take a singular verb.)

n.a: The subject is box, which is singular. "Of sterile gloves" is an intervening phrase and does not change the verb.
n.b: Each is singular, so it takes has even when followed by "of the new students."
n.d: A committee acting as a single unit takes a singular verb in US English.
n.e: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, manager, which is singular.

E.q: In anatomy lab, each pair of students began the dissection of a preserved frog, following the steps in the lab manual. Based on all of its word parts, what does dissection mean?
o: To cut apart a specimen for study
The act of cutting apart for study
The study of how living things work
A tool used to cut apart a specimen
E.w: Step 1: dis- means apart and sect means cut. Step 2: -tion forms a noun naming an act or process. Dissection is the act of cutting something apart (for study).

n.0: This defines the verb dissect; the -tion suffix makes dissection a noun.
n.2: The study of living things is biology (bio + -logy), and the word has no part meaning study.
n.3: -tion names an act or process, not a tool (the tool is a scalpel).

E.q: A nursing journal editor is checking sentences in a research article. Which sentences use bias-free language? Select all that apply.
o: The study enrolled 50 adults confined to wheelchairs.
The study included 40 people with epilepsy.
The study enrolled 50 adults who use wheelchairs.
The new nurse manager, a woman in her 30s, was surprisingly organized.
Each server at the hospital cafe received a holiday bonus.
E.w: Bias-free language puts the person first ("adults who use wheelchairs," "people with epilepsy") and uses gender-neutral titles ("server").

n.0: "Confined to wheelchairs" treats the wheelchair as a limit rather than a tool; use "who use wheelchairs."
n.3: Mentioning gender and age is unnecessary here, and "surprisingly" implies a stereotype.

E.q: After the patient's hip surgery, the doctor prescribed an anticoagulant to take for several weeks. Based on the prefix, what does an anticoagulant do?
o: Measures clotting time
Speeds up blood clotting
Works against blood clotting
Breaks down existing clots
E.w: anti- means against, and coagulant refers to clotting, so an anticoagulant works against the clotting of blood.

n.0: Nothing in the word refers to measuring; a measuring term would use -meter or a test name.
n.1: Speeding up clotting is the opposite of anti- (against).
n.3: Breaking down would be shown by -lysis (as in thrombolysis), not by anti-.

E.q: A writing center handout gives six sentences. Which sentences use semicolons and colons correctly? Select all that apply.
o: The tour visits Dayton, Ohio; Erie, Pennsylvania; and Gary, Indiana.
The forms are: the consent, the history, and the release.
The vote was postponed; because the meeting ran late.
Although the meeting ran late; the vote was held.
The kit has one gap: no sterile gloves.
The meeting ran late; therefore, the vote was postponed.
E.w: A semicolon with a conjunctive adverb joins independent clauses; a colon after a complete clause introduces an explanation; semicolons separate series items that contain commas.

n.1: A colon must not come directly after a verb such as "are".
n.2: "Because the meeting ran late" is a dependent clause; a semicolon must join two independent clauses.
n.3: "Although the meeting ran late" is a dependent clause, so a comma, not a semicolon, should follow it.

E.q: A nurse is writing patient instructions and wants every line to be a complete sentence. Which of the following is a complete sentence?
o: Please sign the consent form before the procedure.
The consent form that was signed before the procedure.
Since the consent form was signed before the procedure.
Signing the consent form before the procedure.
E.w: An imperative sentence is complete even though its subject (you) is not stated: "[You] Please sign the consent form."

n.1: "That was signed ..." is a relative clause describing the form; the subject "The consent form" has no main verb.
n.2: "Since" makes this a dependent clause, which cannot stand alone.
n.3: This is a gerund phrase with no main verb.
